slides.title: First-Class and Higher-Order Functions
slides.prompt: In Python, functions are first-class citizens. This means functions can be passed as arguments, returned from other functions, and assigned to variables. A higher-order function is a function that takes another function as a parameter or returns a function.

slides.title: Function Assignment
slides.prompt: Fill in the correct variable reference to assign the 'say_hello' function without calling it.

slides.title: Higher-Order Function Definition
slides.prompt: Which of the following best defines a Higher-Order Function in Python?
options: A function that accepts another function as an argument or returns a function
A function defined inside a class structure only
A function that uses global variables exclusively
A function that executes with recursive calls
slides.correctAnswer: A function that accepts another function as an argument or returns a function

slides.title: Returning Functions
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to return the inner function from the outer function.

slides.title: Passing Functions as Arguments
slides.prompt: What happens when you pass `len` (without parentheses) to a function as an argument?
options: The function receives a reference to the built-in len function object
It converts len into a string
slides.correctAnswer: The function receives a reference to the built-in len function object

slides.title: Function Inspection
slides.prompt: Fill in the attribute used to check the original name of a function object.
